targeting_context.jd_text:
Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities

    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have

    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have

    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner-facing applied AI architecture) |

## JD Complement
This is a scale-design leadership opportunity at the intersection of enterprise AI adoption, ecosystem leverage, and trust. The central question is how Anthropic can expand Claude through external delivery organizations without
diluting technical quality, customer confidence, or the company’s safety-oriented identity.

The role sits where commercial ambition meets operating discipline. Success depends on helping partners turn broad model capability into customer-ready solutions, while keeping implementation patterns reusable enough to inform the
platform rather than becoming a collection of custom services engagements.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a San Francisco-based public benefit corporation and AI research company. Its market identity combines frontier-model development with enterprise and developer products, framed by a strong commitment to dependable,
understandable, and controllable AI.

Claude is positioned for complex knowledge work, analytical tasks, and software development. That creates an operating model in which product access alone is insufficient: customers also need practical deployment choices, organizational
readiness, governance, and confidence in how AI will be used.

The company’s differentiation is therefore not solely model performance. It also rests on whether enterprise users can adopt AI in ways that feel secure, useful, supportable, and aligned with responsible operating practices.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s safety-centered positioning creates a higher bar for ecosystem execution. Partners must be able to connect business value with disciplined implementation choices, not treat governance as a late-stage compliance exercise.

The company provides a general-purpose AI capability layer rather than a finished workflow for every industry. External partners are important because they bring domain context, integration skills, customer access, and change-management
capacity needed to turn platform capabilities into applied outcomes.

A key pressure is preserving clarity between customer-specific requests and reusable product direction. Commercial teams may seek speed; product, engineering, research, and safety functions must protect coherent platform evolution.
Strong field signals need to be translated into structured evidence rather than anecdotal escalation.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic describes a cross-functional organization spanning research, engineering, policy, and business. Partnership architecture work therefore requires influence across groups with different incentives, vocabulary, and decision
cadence.

Key stakeholder terrain includes:
- Partnerships and commercial teams seeking credible ecosystem capacity, joint account momentum, and repeatable technical differentiation.
- Research, safety, and policy functions shaping the principles partners must reflect in enterprise solution design and customer conversations.
- Customer administrators and technical sponsors responsible for identity, access, rollout planning, user readiness, and expansion decisions.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Claude spans assistant, enterprise, and developer-oriented experiences. Architecture discussions are consequently broader than selecting a model or demonstrating prompts; they include access controls, integration design, operational
readiness, user behavior, measurement, and long-term support.

Anthropic’s enterprise deployment materials frame adoption as a progression from environment setup through launch, enablement, and broader organizational use. That signals a view of implementation in which technical configuration and
business adoption are interdependent.

Enterprise guidance also references administration for coding-related usage. This suggests that developer adoption can be part of a broader governance model, raising the importance of permissions, onboarding, usage visibility, and
technical change management.

The safety and interpretability orientation should be treated as an architectural constraint. The strongest ecosystem patterns will be easy to explain, govern, maintain, and extend—not merely compelling in a short demonstration.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly groups its ecosystem across cloud, technology, and services partners. This indicates a multi-party model in which infrastructure availability, software integration, and delivery expertise must combine to create
enterprise value.

The partner proposition is oriented around solving customer AI challenges rather than simple referral economics. That implies ecosystem maturity will depend on shared solution patterns, technical credibility, implementation readiness,
and coordinated account execution.

Accenture’s public framing of its relationship with Anthropic combines enterprise AI models with industry and technology expertise. It illustrates why strategic partnerships require more than commercial alignment: value emerges when
model capability is translated into practical operating contexts.

Reported investment in the Claude Partner Network, including training and sales-support infrastructure, signals a move toward more systematic ecosystem scale. The next challenge is converting program assets into durable practitioner
capability and consistent customer outcomes.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Expanded partner-program investment increases the importance of execution quality. Training, portals, and playbooks only create leverage when partners can apply them in live enterprise situations with confidence and technical rigor.

The competitive environment extends beyond model vendors. Enterprise buyers can obtain AI capabilities through cloud providers, software platforms, consultancies, and internal development teams. Anthropic’s ecosystem advantage depends
on partners being able to explain where Claude fits and how it can be adopted responsibly.

Enterprise AI demand is also shifting from experimentation toward operational deployment. Customers increasingly evaluate governance, user adoption, measurable value, and sustained usage alongside raw model capability. Partners that
can make those elements repeatable become a material strategic asset.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Designing partner-facing technical motions that can scale beyond bespoke executive involvement.
- Turning broad AI capabilities into reusable enterprise and industry solution patterns.
- Helping service, cloud, and technology partners deliver customer outcomes with consistent operating standards.
- Building structured pathways from deployment learning into product, engineering, and ecosystem planning.
- Pairing commercial urgency with disciplined security, reliability, and responsible-use practices.
- Treating adoption as a combination of technical rollout, user readiness, governance, and expansion planning.
- Aligning sales, partnerships, product, engineering, security, and customer technical stakeholders around common outcomes.
- Establishing practical standards that improve ecosystem consistency without centralizing all delivery work internally.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Claude’s enterprise adoption framing recognizes that successful implementation extends beyond provisioning and initial access.
- Public partner messaging highlights the importance of combining AI capability with industry context and applied implementation expertise.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume/proof graph.
